100: Kino's Journey: The Beautiful World by Keiichi Sigsawa (Vertical) is a quiet, thoughtful fantasy about travel and the people met along the way. Kino rides from country to country on Hermes, a talking motorcycle, and never stays anywhere longer than three days. Each stop has its own strange customs, kind or cruel, and Kino mostly watches and moves on. It suits readers who like short, reflective stories that leave something to think about.
102: Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You by Jinushi (Square Enix Manga) is a gentle comedy about two tired adults finding a little comfort. Sasaki, a worn-out office worker, looks forward to buying groceries from Yamada, the cheerful cashier at his local supermarket. One night he starts sharing smoke breaks out back with a blunt woman named Tayama, never guessing she is the same cashier out of uniform. It's a sweet, low-key read for grown-ups who like slow-burn romance.
105: Men of the Harem by Alphatart (Ize Press) is a romantic court fantasy full of scheming and politics. Latil becomes the first female emperor of her country, but her throne is shaky and her heart is still bruised from a past love. To win allies and secure her rule, she decides to build a harem of handsome, powerful men. Meanwhile, rumors spread that a legendary dark lord is about to return. It's a great pick for fans of palace intrigue and dramatic romance.
108: Mushishi by Yuki Urushibara (Del Rey) is a calm, atmospheric supernatural story set in a quiet, old-fashioned Japan. Ginko is a mushi master, a wanderer who studies mushi, simple life forms that most people can't see but that can cause strange illnesses and odd happenings. He travels from village to village, helping people whose lives have been touched by them. Each chapter stands mostly on its own, making it a lovely, unhurried read for fans of folklore and quiet mysteries.
110: There's No Freaking Way I'll Be Your Lover! Unless... by Teren Mikami (Seven Seas) is a bubbly yuri romantic comedy. Renako Amaori worked hard to reinvent herself and finally fit in with the popular crowd in high school. Then Mai Oduka, the most dazzling girl in school, confesses to her. Renako insists she only wants to be friends, so Mai makes a bet that she can win her over. It's fun, flustered, and perfect for readers who enjoy silly, sweet romance.
111: Sugar Apple Fairy Tale by Miri Mikawa (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy romance about chasing a dream. Anne Halford wants to become a silver sugar master, an artist who crafts candy sculptures that carry real meaning in her kingdom. To travel to the royal capital for an important competition, she buys a warrior fairy named Challe to serve as her bodyguard, even though she hates the idea of owning a fairy. It's warm and charming, with a slow-building bond at its heart.
112: I Got Married to the Girl I Hate Most in Class by Amano Seiju (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about rivals stuck under one roof. Saito Hojo and Akane Sakuramori are top students who can't stand each other and argue constantly. Then their grandparents arrange for the two of them to marry and live together. Now they have to share a home while keeping it secret from their classmates. It's a light, funny read for fans of bickering couples and slow-warming feelings.
118: The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Shadows by Sakaku Hishikawa (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy light novel with a big heart and a dry sense of humor. Zenos grew up in the slums and taught himself healing magic, but his adventuring party kicks him out for being too low-born. Rather than give up, he opens an unlicensed clinic in the slums, where his skills turn out to be far greater than anyone guessed. It's a cozy underdog story for readers who like found-family fantasy.
122: Issak by Shinji Makari and Double-S (Kodansha) is a gritty historical action story set in 17th-century Europe. During the Thirty Years' War, a quiet Japanese mercenary arrives in Germany carrying a matchlock rifle of remarkable accuracy. Known as Issak, he joins the fighting while hunting a man he has followed across the world. It's a tense, well-researched read for fans of war stories, sharpshooters, and samurai tales told far from home.
125: The Climber by Shin-ichi Sakamoto (Seven Seas) is an intense, beautifully drawn drama about one young man and the mountains. Buntaro Mori is a lonely, withdrawn transfer student until a classmate dares him to climb the outside of their school building. That climb awakens something in him, and he begins pushing himself toward harder and more dangerous ascents. Based on a novel by Jiro Nitta, it's a striking pick for readers who like serious, character-driven sports stories.
126: Ossan Idol! by Mochiko Mochida (Tokyopop) is a cheerful comedy about starting over in middle age. Nobuo Mineyama is a 40-something office worker who decides it's time to get in shape. When videos of his workouts and dancing start getting attention online, he finds himself on an unlikely path toward becoming an idol. It's an upbeat, feel-good read for anyone who likes stories about chasing something new at any age.
129: Flowers and Bees by Moyoco Anno (Viz Media) is a sharp, silly comedy about wanting to be cool. Masao Komatsu is an awkward high school boy desperate to become attractive and finally get a girlfriend. He wanders into a men's beauty salon run by two glamorous, merciless sisters, who take him on as their latest project. What follows is a string of humiliating makeovers. It's a fun read for fans of over-the-top teen comedy.
132: Absolute Boyfriend by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a sci-fi twist. Riiko Izawa has terrible luck with boys, so when she stumbles onto a website selling the perfect boyfriend, she gives it a try. A box soon arrives with Night, a lifelike robot designed to love her completely. Then comes the bill for the trial, and it's far more than she can pay. It's a playful, heartfelt read for longtime shojo fans.
133: Aishiteruze Baby by Yoko Maki (Viz Media) is a sweet, funny shojo story about growing up by taking care of someone else. Kippei Katakura is a carefree high school flirt with no interest in responsibility. Then his five-year-old cousin Yuzuyu comes to live with his family after her mother leaves, and Kippei is put in charge of looking after her. It's tender and warmhearted, a good pick for readers who love family stories with a light touch.
135: Monster Musume by OKAYADO (Seven Seas) is a goofy, fan-service-heavy comedy for older teens and adults. Kimihito Kurusu is an ordinary young man who ends up as a host family under a government program that brings mythical species into human society. His first guest is Miia, a lamia who is half woman and half snake, and more monster girls soon move in. It's a light, cheeky read for fans of harem comedy.
138: That Wolf-Boy Is Mine! by Yoko Nogiri (Kodansha) is a light shojo romance with a supernatural twist. Komugi Inugami has just transferred to a new high school in Hokkaido and is hoping to make friends. She's drawn to her quiet classmate Yu Sakuraba, then discovers his secret: he can turn into a wolf. Soon she learns he isn't the only shapeshifter at school. It's a cute, cozy series for readers who like gentle romance and fluffy animal charm.
140: The All-New Tenchi Muyo! by Hitoshi Okuda (Viz Media) is a lighthearted sci-fi comedy based on the long-running anime. Tenchi Masaki is a regular teenager whose quiet country home has been overrun by alien women, including the wild space pirate Ryoko and the proud princess Ayeka. Between rivalries, space visitors, and household chaos, Tenchi rarely gets a moment's peace. It's a fun pick for fans of the anime and classic harem comedy.
141: Angelic Layer by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a bright, energetic action story about a game and the friends made through it. Misaki Suzuhara moves to Tokyo and discovers Angelic Layer, a popular game where players control small dolls called Angels with their minds and battle in an arena. Small for her age but full of spirit, Misaki builds her own Angel, Hikaru, and jumps into competition. It's a lively read for fans of tournament stories and CLAMP's art.
144: My Status as an Assassin Obviously Exceeds the Hero's by Matsuri Akai (Seven Seas) is a darker take on the summoned-to-another-world fantasy. Akira Oda is a quiet student who gets transported to a fantasy kingdom along with his entire class. Assigned the class of Assassin, he finds his stats are far stronger than those of the classmate named the Hero. When Akira learns the kingdom isn't what it seems, he slips into the shadows to uncover the truth. It suits fans of isekai with an edge.
146: Aria by Kozue Amano (ADV) is a peaceful, slice-of-life science fiction story set on a future Mars covered in water. In the city of Neo-Venezia, Akari Mizunashi is training to become an Undine, a gondolier who guides tourists through the canals. Each chapter follows her small adventures, new friendships, and quiet discoveries around town. It's a soothing, gently beautiful read for anyone who wants a calm, comforting story.
147: Negima!? Neo by Ken Akamatsu (Kodansha) is a lively magical comedy that reimagines the world of Negima! Magister Negi Magi. Negi Springfield is a ten-year-old wizard sent to Japan to teach a class of rowdy middle school girls, all while keeping his magic a secret. This spin-off retells his adventures with a lighter, sillier spin. It's a fun extra for fans of the original series and its huge cast.
148: Attack on Titan Colossal Edition by Hajime Isayama (Kodansha) collects the dark fantasy action series in oversized omnibus volumes. Humanity survives behind enormous walls, hiding from Titans, giant humanlike creatures that devour people. When a colossal Titan breaks through the wall of his hometown, young Eren Yeager vows to fight back. It's tense, grim, and gripping, and these big editions are a great way for fans to own or revisit the series.
149: The Faraway Paladin Omnibus by Kanata Yanagino (J-Novel Club) is a warm, thoughtful fantasy about family and second chances. After an unhappy life, a young man is reborn in a world of swords and magic as a baby named Will. He is raised in a ruined city by three undead guardians: a skeleton warrior, a mummified priestess, and a ghostly sorcerer. As Will grows, he begins to wonder why they're there. It's a heartfelt read for fans of classic fantasy adventure.
152: The Good Witch of the West by Noriko Ogiwara and Haruhiko Momokawa (Tokyopop) is a romantic fantasy with court intrigue. Firiel Dee is a cheerful country girl and the daughter of a reclusive astronomer. On her fifteenth birthday she receives her late mother's necklace, and wearing it to her first ball reveals that she may be in line for the throne. Suddenly she's caught up in royal politics and danger. It's a fun read for fans of classic shojo fantasy.
153: Hetalia: Axis Powers by Hidekaz Himaruya (Tokyopop) is a goofy comedy that turns world history into a cast of quirky characters. Each country is a person: Italy is a cheerful, pasta-loving slacker, Germany is his stern and serious friend, and Japan is polite and reserved. Their short, silly adventures poke fun at national stereotypes and real historical events. It's a quick, playful read for history buffs and anyone who likes gag comedy.
154: The Hero Is Overpowered but Overly Cautious by Light Tuchihi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy that pokes fun at the usual hero story. The goddess Ristarte summons Seiya Ryuguin to save a very dangerous world, and he turns out to be incredibly strong. The trouble is that he's also incredibly cautious, insisting on endless training and preparing for every possible threat, no matter how small. It's a funny, fast read for fans of isekai parody.
161: Orc Eroica by Rifujin na Magonote (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel with a surprisingly earnest hero. Bash is the greatest warrior the orcs have ever known, a hero of the recent war. In orc society, though, being a virgin is a mark of shame, and Bash has never had a partner. Now that peace has come, he sets out to find a wife, honorably, which proves harder than any battle. It's a goofy, good-natured read from the author of Mushoku Tensei.
169: The Seven Deadly Sins Omnibus by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) collects the action fantasy series in larger, value-packed volumes. The Seven Deadly Sins were once a band of legendary knights, until they were accused of treason and scattered. Princess Elizabeth sets out to find them to save her kingdom and stumbles into a tavern run by Meliodas, a cheerful young man with a talking pig. It's fun, fast-moving adventure for shonen fans.
171: Idol Dreams by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a romantic drama about getting a second chance at youth. Chikage Ichinose is a 31-year-old office worker who feels she missed out on love and fun as a teenager. When a mysterious pill makes her look fifteen again, she seizes the chance and ends up stepping into the world of idols. It's sweet, a bit bittersweet, and great for readers who like grown-up heroines.
173: The Tarot Cafe by Sang-Sun Park (Tokyopop) is a dark, dreamy fantasy manhwa told through supernatural stories. Pamela runs a small tarot shop, and her most important clients come at night: werewolves, fairies, witches, and other creatures seeking answers. Each reading reveals a story of love, loss, or regret, while Pamela keeps a long-held secret of her own. It's a moody, gothic read for fans of folklore and beautiful art.
174: Peacemaker Kurogane by Nanae Chrono (Tokyopop) is a historical action story set in the final years of the samurai. Tetsunosuke Ichimura is a short-tempered teen who wants revenge for the murder of his parents. Hoping to become strong, he joins the Shinsengumi, the famous police force of Kyoto, where he finds both friendship and danger. It's a lively blend of humor and drama for fans of samurai stories.
175: Imadoki! by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a gentle shojo comedy about staying true to yourself. Tanpopo Yamazaki moves from the countryside to attend Meio Academy, an elite school full of rich kids who mostly ignore her. Determined to make friends, she decides to start a gardening committee, and along the way she gets to know Koki, a boy who isn't quite what he seems. It's a sweet, upbeat read about kindness and growing roots.
177: Brave Story by Miyuki Miyabe (Viz Media) is a heartfelt fantasy adventure about a boy facing hard times. Eleven-year-old Wataru Mitani's ordinary life falls apart when his family is torn apart. When a mysterious door opens into a magical world called Vision, Wataru learns that whoever completes a quest there may change their fate. He sets out on a journey full of danger and new friends. It's a strong pick for fans of classic quest stories.
180: In the Land of Leadale by Ceez (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy about waking up in a game world. After a long illness, Keina passes away and wakes up as Cayna, her high elf character from the VR game she loved. The world looks like Leadale, but two hundred years have passed, and her old friends and creations have changed. It's a relaxing, gentle isekai for readers who prefer exploration and found family to big battles.
182: Candy Color Paradox by Isaku Natsume (SuBLime) is a lively boys' love romance set in the world of tabloid journalism. Onoe is a hardworking reporter who gets transferred to a gossip magazine and paired with Kaburagi, a skilled but cocky photographer. The two clash constantly as they stake out celebrity scandals, but long nights together start to change things. It's a fun, funny pick for fans of rivals-to-lovers BL.
184: Irina: The Vampire Cosmonaut by Keisuke Makino (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi romance light novel set during an alternate Cold War space race. Lev Leps is a cosmonaut candidate in a nation desperate to reach space first. He is assigned to supervise Irina Luminesk, a vampire chosen as a test subject to be sent into orbit before any human. It's a touching, slow-burn story for readers who like romance mixed with history and science.
187: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle by Hiromu (Yen Press) is a high school romance and drama with a popular kid at its center. Saku Chitose is at the top of his school's social ladder, handsome, confident, and surrounded by friends. One day his teacher asks him to help Kenta, a shut-in classmate, return to school. Saku takes on the job in his own way. It's a thoughtful read for fans of character-driven school stories.
192: Combatants Will Be Dispatched! by Natsume Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a sci-fi comedy light novel from the creator of KonoSuba. Combatant Agent Six works for the Kisaragi Corporation, an evil secret organization bent on world domination. He is sent to an alien planet to scout it for invasion, along with a high-tech android partner. Once there, he gets caught up in a fantasy kingdom's war. It's silly, rowdy fun for fans of comedy that doesn't take itself seriously.
197: Ran and the Gray World by Aki Irie (Viz Media) is a whimsical, beautifully drawn fantasy about growing up. Ran Uruma is a ten-year-old girl from a family of magic users, and she can't wait to be an adult. By slipping on her mother's magic sneakers, she can turn into a grown woman for a while, though she's still a kid inside. It's a charming, imaginative read for fans of gentle magical stories.
